maya (runtime): uploaded the perfetto trace from yesterday's canary run: https://perfetto.example/trace/1772504821 — main symptom: intermittent 60-200ms queue spikes with small batches (batch_size 1-4).

sam (kernel): looking now. did you capture nsys/nvprof too or just perfetto?

maya (runtime): perfetto + minimal nsys capture. nvprof was noisy for the short windows. I pulled a flamechart — most time is in `fused_attn_qkv` kernel and in a long `cudaMemcpyAsync` at the start of some windows.

ali (infra): can you paste the perfetto time ranges? I want to correlate with our scheduler logs.

maya (runtime): ranges: [00:01:12 - 00:01:14], [00:09:03 - 00:09:06], [00:26:58 - 00:27:01] — queueTime spikes ~80-180ms, computeTime stable ~12-20ms.

julia (sre): that smells like batching window underflow — we expect continuous batching to hold requests for up to `batch_window_ms`, but if KV cache hits return quickly they could trigger small batches.

sam (kernel): also check kernel selection path. On small seq len the runtime sometimes picks the quantized matmul kernel which has higher startup overhead but lower per-token cost. With tiny batches that overhead dominates.

maya (runtime): confirmed: kernel selector logs show fallback to `qmatmul_v2` for seq<=32 and dynamic_unfused for a few shards. For the big spikes the selector switched mid-run because `estimated_tokens` logic read from stale model profile.

tracebot: nsys summary uploaded: https://ci.example/nsys/1772504821-summary — hotspot: `fused_attn_qkv` (42%), `qmatmul_init` (28%), `kv_cache_write` (6%).

ali (infra): I matched perfetto slices to infra scheduler: during the spikes the GPU was under light contention, but the host-side queue had bursts of many tiny pending requests (10-30 in 200ms). Looks like our dequeue algorithm batches by age-first which can create a long waiting tail.

sam (kernel): possible fixes: 1) change kernel selector cost model to include batch startup cost, 2) adjust continuous batching to prefer filling by count for <5ms windows, 3) pre-warm qmatmul kernel (keep alive) when usage is expected.

maya (runtime): tried a local patch to pre-warm qmatmul (launch an init kernel) — perfetto shows warmup reduced `qmatmul_init` from 80ms to 6ms but introduced a small steady 2ms overhead per-instance. Might be worth for latency SLO.

julia (sre): tradeoff looks acceptable for p95. For p50 maybe regresses slightly. Need telemetry to flag rollout.

ali (infra): scheduling tweak we can A/B: in the enqueue path, if pending queue depth > threshold, switch to count-based flushing for N ms; otherwise keep age-based. This should reduce tail waiting.

maya (runtime): I also noticed KV cache behavior: when cache hits are high, response generation returns earlier and creates tiny follow-on requests for rerank/token edits — these re-enter queue and are batched poorly. We should tag cache-hot requests to use a fast-path queue that prefers grouping similar prefixes.

sam (kernel): agree. Also add a micro-benchmark in CI: a perfetto trace for ramping 1->50 qps with mixed KV hit rates. We can assert queueTime < X and kernel init < Y.

julia (sre): action items:
- maya: instrument kernel selector with `startup_cost` and expose a heatmap (due EOD + link).
- ali: implement count-based fallback in scheduler (PR + perf test, due tomorrow).
- sam: add CI micro-benchmark and pre-warm experiment (RFC by EOD).

maya (runtime): I've pushed a draft log patch: `git diff -- perf/runtime/selector.cpp` snippet:
```
+ // account for startup cost measured from perf experiments
+ float effective_cost = base_cost + startup_cost / max(1, batch_size);
```

ali (infra): I'll run a controlled canary with both patches next deploy window. I'll attach perfetto + nsys for correlation.

sam (kernel): saved the trace and will dig into kernel timeline to see if we can fuse the init path further.

maya (runtime): thanks — will update thread with links when I upload the heatmap. For now perfetto + nsys links above; nvprof was discarded. :thumbsup:

julia (sre): please add a dashboard card for queueTime vs computeTime split so on-call can spot regressions automatically.

maya (runtime): noted. I'll create ticket INF-2147 and link results.
